tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Non-Conviction Records Pursuant to Pa.R.Crim.P. 790
tracks.publicName: Expunge a Pennsylvania court case that did not end in a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 9122(a) requires expungement of criminal history record information where no disposition has been received or recorded within 18 months after the date of arrest and the court finds the conditions met, or where a court order requires nonconviction data to be expunged. Rule 790 prescribes the petition contents, the attached Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report, service on the attorney for the Commonwealth, and the expungement order for court cases.

exclusions: Mixed cases in which any charge in the case resulted in a conviction. Section 9122(a) reaches nonconviction data; a case with a conviction on any count is not a clean non-conviction.
Cases in which only summary offenses were filed and the case remained at the magisterial district court, which proceed under Pa.R.Crim.P. 490 instead.
Records held by federal, military, tribal or out-of-state authorities, which Pennsylvania relief does not reach.

rules.filing: File the verified Rule 790 petition, the blank expungement order and the attached Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report with the clerk of the courts of the judicial district in which the charges were disposed.
rules.fees: County filing fees vary and are not established by statute. The legal review reports a range of roughly $132 to $215 across counties, with expungement petitions generally costing more than limited access petitions. No confirmed statewide schedule exists.
rules.feeWaiver: In forma pauperis relief is available; the Court of Common Pleas Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis is published statewide. It is CPCMS 2046 (two pages, financial questions, an unsworn-falsification verification under 18 Pa.C.S. § 4904 rather than a notary block; no new printed revision date asserted), held in custody as PA-IFP-CCP (sha256 b1255ef0503f…). When the participant selects the fee-waiver branch the motion is rendered as part of the packet, not merely retained as source evidence: only the participant's actual financial information is written, no financial zeros are invented, the verification is never executed for the participant, and public-access-policy compliance is not marked without performing the applicable checks. The judge decides the request; submitting it is not an approval. If no waiver is requested the conditional exclusion is preserved. (Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research.)
rules.notice: A copy of the petition is served on the attorney for the Commonwealth concurrently with filing. Within 60 days after service the attorney for the Commonwealth shall file a consent or objection to the petition or take no action.
rules.service: Service on the attorney for the Commonwealth concurrently with filing, per Pa.R.Crim.P. 790. Rule 790's Comment directs filing and service to Rule 576 and treats the petition as a motion for Rules 575–577, so the paper-service method is supplied by rule, not an unanswerable local-law question: Rule 576 methods include mailing a copy to the party's attorney; a copy is also served on the court administrator by the methods Rule 576 lists; a signed certificate of service records the date and manner of service and each recipient's name, address and telephone number; electronic filing follows Rule 576.1 rather than assuming an emailed document accomplishes service. Current recipient addresses and any e-filing choice remain local inputs, and service facts are completed after service, never pre-certified. (Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research; previously stated only the Rule 790 recipient and timing.)
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and verifies the petition.
rules.proposedOrder: The blank expungement order (PA-RCRIM-P-790-ORDER) is optional, not a filing prerequisite: the AOPC public-forms page expressly says the proposed order is not mandatory (PA3). It may remain in the packet as a convenience, correctly labeled optional, with the court's blocks left blank. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research.

researchCertificateSpecimen.use: Proposed completion content for the existing composed certificate of service, not a newly accepted official form: original caption and docket number; a body certifying service on an actual date of an identified document on the listed recipients by the method recorded for each; a recipient table (attorney for the Commonwealth, court administrator, other party if applicable) with verified address, telephone number and the method actually used; signature of the unrepresented petitioner. Service is never pre-certified; no fictional recipients or numbers.

researchParticipantText.text:
Filing and service. File the Rule 790 petition with the clerk of courts in the judicial district where the charges were disposed. Serve the attorney for the Commonwealth at the same time. Follow Rule 576 for the method, service on the court administrator, and the certificate documenting actual service. Mailing to the proper attorney's office is an available paper-service method. Confirm the recipients' current addresses; follow the applicable electronic-filing rule when filing electronically.

Order and costs. The blank proposed order is optional, not a filing prerequisite. Confirm the filing charge with the filing office. When requesting permission to proceed without paying because you cannot afford the fee, complete and submit the Common Pleas Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis. Use your actual financial information. The judge decides the request; submitting it is not an approval.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The highest-volume and cleanest Pennsylvania track. Section 9122(a) is mandatory on its terms, Rule 790 prescribes the petition contents, and the statewide petition and order are retained by Edition 1.2 and checksum-verified. The 18-month no-disposition route, which the review could not confirm against the statute, is confirmed in the current official text of § 9122(a) and is carried as a distinct eligibility branch with its own clock rather than merged into the ordinary non-conviction route.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Non-Conviction Summary Case Records Pursuant to Pa.R.Crim.P. 490
tracks.publicName: Expunge a Pennsylvania summary case that did not end in a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Rule 490 governs expungement in summary cases. Any case in which a summary offense was filed together with a misdemeanor, felony or murder charge proceeds under Rule 790 instead. The rule prescribes the petition contents, the attached Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing, service on the attorney for the Commonwealth, and the expungement order.

exclusions: Any case in which a summary offense was filed together with a misdemeanor, felony or murder charge. Rule 490 expressly routes those cases to Rule 790.
Cases that moved to the court of common pleas.
Mixed cases in which any charge resulted in a conviction.

tracks.publicName: Check that a full acquittal cleared your record automatically

controllingAuthority.summary: Where a person is acquitted of all charges based on the same conduct or arising from the same criminal episode, § 9122(a) provides for expungement without a petition. The Commonwealth has 60 days to object and, where the statutory requirements are met, expungement occurs no later than 12 months from the date of acquittal.

exclusions: Partial acquittals. A person acquitted on some counts and convicted or otherwise disposed on others is outside this route entirely and is screened under the Rule 790 non-conviction track or the petition-based limited access track.
Cases where the acquitted and non-acquitted charges arose from different conduct or different criminal episodes.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Summary Conviction After Five Arrest-Free Years
tracks.publicName: Expunge an old Pennsylvania summary conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 9122(b) permits a court to order expungement of a summary offence conviction where the person has been free of arrest or prosecution for five years following the conviction. The petition is made on the Rule 490 or Rule 790 form depending on the court in which the case was disposed.

exclusions: Any arrest or prosecution during the five-year period, even where it did not result in a conviction. The § 9122(b) standard is free of arrest or prosecution, which is stricter than the conviction-free standards used by limited access and Clean Slate.
Misdemeanour and felony convictions, which have no § 9122(b) expungement route.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of the Arrest Record on Successful Completion of Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition
tracks.publicName: Check that finishing ARD cleared your arrest record

controllingAuthority.summary: When the judge orders dismissal of the charges after successful completion of Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition, Rule 320 provides that the judge also shall order expungement of the defendant's arrest record, subject to a Commonwealth objection filed within 30 days after service of the motion for dismissal, on which the Commonwealth must show compelling reasons to retain the record. Section 9122(b.1) removes the court's authority to expunge the arrest record where ARD was granted for enumerated sexual offences and the victim was under 18.

exclusions: ARD granted for an offence under 18 Pa.C.S. §§ 3121 through 3127, § 5902(b) or § 5903 where the victim was under 18 years of age. Section 9122(b.1) removes the court's authority to expunge the arrest record in those cases.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Order for Limited Access Under 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122.1
tracks.publicName: Petition to seal a Pennsylvania conviction from public view

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 9122.1(a) permits a petition for limited access to a qualifying misdemeanour or ungraded offence carrying a maximum penalty of no more than five years where the person has been free from conviction for a period of seven years, has completed all court-ordered restitution, and has paid the authorized fee. Section 9122.1(a.1), added by Act 36 of 2023, extends the petition to qualifying felonies other than felonies of the first and second degree where the person has been free from conviction for a period of ten years on the same conditions. Rule 791 prescribes the petition, the attached Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing, service on the attorney for the Commonwealth, and the order.

exclusions: Offences punishable by more than two years in the following categories, per § 9122.1(b): offences involving danger to the person under Article B of Part II; offences against the family under Article D; firearms and other dangerous articles under Chapter 61; offences requiring registration under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9799.14 or § 9799.55; and corruption of minors.

Prior-record bars under § 9122.1(b)(2): a conviction for murder or a felony of the first degree; certain serious offences within the preceding 15 years; and two or more offences punishable by more than two years within the preceding 10 years.
Felonies of the first and second degree, which are outside the § 9122.1(a.1) qualifying-felony route.
A drug felony on which a minimum sentence of 30 months or more, or a maximum sentence of 60 months or more, was imposed, which falls outside the § 9102 definition of qualifying offence.

tracks.publicName: Check whether Clean Slate has sealed your record automatically

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 9122.2 provides automatic limited access without any petition. Subsection (a)(1) reaches a conviction of a misdemeanour of the second degree or a misdemeanour punishable by no more than two years where the person has been free for seven years from conviction for any offence punishable by imprisonment of one or more years. Subsection (a)(1.1) reaches a qualifying offence on the same terms after ten years. Subsection (a)(2) reaches charges resulting in a final disposition other than a conviction. Subsection (a)(3) reaches a summary conviction when five years have elapsed since entry of the judgment of conviction. Subsection (a)(4) reaches a conviction for which a conditional pardon was granted. Under subsection (b) the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts transmits eligible records to the Pennsylvania State Police central repository and removes records for which a notification of ineligibility is received.

exclusions: The exclusions in § 9122.3 are keyed by subsection rather than expressed as one generic ineligible-offence list. Section 9122.3(a) states that limited access under § 9122.2(a)(1) shall not be granted for the enumerated categories, and § 9122.3(a)(2) carries its own separate structure; § 9122.3(c) provides that an offence eligible for clean slate limited access is also eligible for a petition for limited access under § 9122.1. The subsection-specific structure is preserved and is not collapsed.
Offences requiring registration under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9799.14 or § 9799.55, and failure to comply with registration requirements under 18 Pa.C.S. § 4915.1, per § 9122.3(a)(1)(iv) and (a)(2)(iv)(C).
An otherwise qualifying conviction where a conviction punishable by five or more years, or another excluded offence, arose out of the same case, except for a qualifying offence.

tracks.publicName: Fix a record that should have been sealed automatically but was not

controllingAuthority.summary: Where an eligible record does not receive limited access through the automatic Clean Slate process, secondary sources indicate the person may need to act to correct it, presumably by petition under Pa.R.Crim.P. 791. The statutory or rule basis for a correction route was not confirmed by the controlling review, and the current official text of § 9122.2 describes the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts and Pennsylvania State Police transmission and ineligibility-notification procedure without establishing a participant-facing correction vehicle.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The controlling review states that the statutory or rule basis for a Clean Slate correction route was not confirmed and that the output strategy is undetermined pending the correction mechanism. The bounded current-primary-authority research carried out for this normalization read 18 Pa.C.S. §§ 9102, 9122, 9122.1, 9122.2, 9122.3 and 9122.5 and Pa.R.Crim.P. 320, 490, 790 and 791 at their official sources. Section 9122.2(b) establishes only the AOPC-to-Pennsylvania State Police transmission and the removal of records for which a notification of ineligibility is received; it creates no participant-facing correction petition, request or form, and Rule 791 on its face governs a petition for limited access rather than the correction of a failed automatic sealing. The review's own suggestion that correction proceeds 'presumably by petition under Rule 791' is expressly a presumption. No output strategy is assigned and no correction petition is invented. The route is deferred so that the ten fully representable Pennsylvania mechanisms are not held back by it.

limitations.statement: The governing mechanism for correcting a Clean Slate automatic sealing failure is undetermined. No participant-facing filing vehicle is established by the controlling review or by the current official text of 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122.2, so this track is deferred rather than built.
